title: server2 host log pipeline: install, select destinations, read logs, prepare AWS, watch for loss, start new instances unattended
scenario: An operator installs the server2 log collector on a Linux host, keeps the default local journal, recovers from a mistyped setting, ships the log to S3 and CloudWatch Logs with different levels, reads each destination, renders the AWS templates (LP-5) that the owner applies, watches one destination fail and recover (LP-2), and starts a new instance from the boot configuration alone (LP-3). Captured on 2026-11-14 in a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 VM (systemd 255) with the pinned Vector 0.61.0 collector and a server2 release binary; S3 and CloudWatch Logs were the loopback stand-in server2/deploy/logging/standin.py, reached through the real regional AWS host names; for step 8 a second, new VM had nothing installed, and instance metadata (instance ID, life cycle, instance-role credentials) was the stand-in server2/deploy/logging/imds_standin.py. All values are synthetic. Full reference: docs/operations/server2-logging.md, section Host log pipeline.

steps.title: Install the pipeline; the default ships nothing
steps.instruction: As root, run server2/deploy/logging/install.sh (with --collector-tarball for a local copy of the pinned archive, otherwise it downloads it). It checks the archive hash, installs the units and enables them. With no SERVER2_LOG_SINKS setting, start both units and check the collector.
steps.caption: install.sh reports the collector version. server2.service is active; server2-logs.service is skipped by its start condition and says why in the server2 journal.
steps.expected: The server runs and writes to the local journal namespace server2. The collector is skipped (start condition unmet), so nothing leaves the host.

steps.title: A mistyped setting fails only the collector
steps.instruction: Set SERVER2_LOG_SINKS in /opt/server2/config/.env (here with a typo, clodwatch) and start the units. Read the collector's message in the server2 journal namespace, fix the value, and start the collector again.
steps.caption: The collector is failed and names SERVER2_LOG_SINKS and the allowed values, without repeating the mistyped value. The server is active and /health answers 200.
steps.expected: server2-logs.service is failed without restarting in a loop; server2.service keeps serving.

steps.title: Ship to S3 and CloudWatch Logs with different levels
steps.instruction: Set the destinations, the per-destination levels, the S3 prefix and an existing CloudWatch log group in .env, then start (or restart) the collector. On EC2 the credentials come from the instance role.
steps.caption: Both units are active. The collector's first record names its version, the active destinations, the host and the boot. This capture predates LP-3: the record now also carries instance_life_cycle, and the host is the EC2 instance ID (the machine ID, as here, only without instance metadata); see step 8.
steps.expected: The collector start record appears in the journal and is shipped to every remote destination.

steps.title: Where records arrive
steps.instruction: Serve requests, then stop the server and the collector (systemctl stop server2.service server2-logs.service stops the server first). The collector's stop waits until every destination has confirmed the records (up to about 60 s for an open S3 object). Look at what arrived: S3 keys under the prefix and CloudWatch streams in the group.
steps.caption: S3 keys and CloudWatch streams carry the source (server or collector), the host ID and the boot ID; S3 keys also carry the UTC date and hour and a unique suffix.
steps.expected: Server and collector records are kept apart, and records from different hosts or boots never share a stream or key.

steps.title: Read each destination
steps.instruction: Read the local journal with journalctl --namespace=server2, an S3 object with gzip -dc (after aws s3 cp), and the CloudWatch stream (aws logs tail on EC2). Filter with jq.
steps.caption: The readiness line stays in the journal only. S3 (level info) holds the info and warn records; CloudWatch (level warn) holds only the two warn records of the HTTP 501 request.
steps.expected: Each destination holds exactly the server records at or above its level, as the original lines.

steps.title: Prepare the AWS templates (LP-5)
steps.instruction: Render the role policy, bucket lifecycle and log group templates for the actual bucket, prefix, group, region and account with server2/deploy/logging/aws_templates.py. Then apply them with administrator credentials using the commands in the guide (section Prepare AWS for the destinations); put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration replaces the whole configuration, so read it first. The capture shows synthetic names; nothing was applied to AWS.
steps.caption: A prefix inside a weather data prefix is refused and nothing is written. The rendered policy grants only PutObject under the log prefix, stream creation, event writing and stream lookup in the one group; the lifecycle covers only the log prefix; the group keeps 30 days.
steps.expected: Three JSON files without placeholders, ready for the owner to apply and read back.

steps.title: Watch a destination fail and recover (LP-2)
steps.instruction: Read the collector's counters on the host (curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9598/metrics) and its status record, written every 60 s to the server2 journal and shipped to every destination. A destination whose oldest unconfirmed record is older than twice its delivery window (S3 120 s, CloudWatch 20 s) is shown as behind. The capture makes S3 fail with the stand-in's fault switch for over two minutes while CloudWatch keeps working, then lets it recover.
steps.caption: While S3 fails, the collector keeps retrying, so its failure counter stays at zero; the status record is warn with s3 behind (134 s unconfirmed) and CloudWatch current. After recovery the records written meanwhile arrive from the journal and the status is info again. The counters listen on 127.0.0.1 only.
steps.expected: An outage is visible in the status record while it lasts, and recovery needs no action.

steps.title: Start a new instance from the boot configuration (LP-3)
steps.instruction: Generate the user data with boot.py for a commit that is on GitHub (normally the merged master commit) and the destination settings, and give user-data.sh.gz to the launch template or instance. At the first boot it downloads the pipeline files from that commit, refuses any file whose SHA-256 differs, installs the pinned collector and starts it; the release procedure then installs server2 and its .env. Nobody logs in, and the instance holds no AWS key.
steps.caption: The user data names the commit and each file's hash (about 1.3 KB of EC2's 16 KB). On the new instance both units are enabled, the collector runs, the destination settings are a unit drop-in, and the start record names the EC2 instance ID, its life cycle and the boot.
steps.expected: The collector ships from its first record; every instance of the launch template uses the same user data and writes its own streams and keys.
